## Recorded output

The code example was executed in the `course-dev` Docker container with
working directory `/workspace`. The payload and envelope metadata are synthetic
and the AES keys and localhost certificate are generated only for the run.

```text
Round trip: True
Ciphertext bytes including tag: 41
changed ciphertext rejected
changed metadata rejected
DEK recovered: True
same DEK after KEK rotation: True
Certificate required: True
Hostname checking: True
Minimum protocol: TLSv1_2
TLS loopback handshake: PASS
TLS negotiated version: TLSv1.3
wrong hostname rejected: True
browser -> gateway: TLS required
gateway -> search: TLS required
search -> worker: GAP TO REVIEW
worker -> storage: TLS required
CHAPTER 10 ENCRYPTION AND TRANSPORT SMOKE TEST PASSED
```

The complete Docker terminal capture is available at
`outputs/encryption_transport_terminal.txt`, and the compact program output is
at `outputs/encryption_transport_output.txt`.

The loopback certificate and private key are created in a temporary directory,
used for the local handshake, and removed automatically. No key, certificate,
KMS credential, or production secret is part of this repository.

## Evidence status

| Status | Result |
|---|---|
| Configured control | AES-GCM authenticated encryption, DEK/KEK envelope, TLS 1.2 minimum, and hostname validation |
| Tested control | Round trip, tamper rejection, key re-wrap, verified loopback TLS, and wrong-host rejection — PASS |
| Failed control | The fictional search-to-worker hop is intentionally recorded as `GAP TO REVIEW` |
| Untested control | KMS access, HDFS encryption zones, external certificate chain, mutual TLS, rotation migration, and every production hop |
| Residual risk | Ephemeral local keys and a self-signed certificate do not establish production key custody or trust |
